answer: An agent first seals collateral in a glacier escrow that calves only after two epochs. Eligibility then requires a wander of eight independently owned falcon perches, each limited to a published vouch cap and required to cut a one-time sighting binding the agent's work leaf to that operator's rotating molt key. When the escrow calves, settlement voids excess vouches and slashes glacier stake of any cluster that shared a perch host, molt-key family, or path-timing skeleton, so a cheap cloned flock cannot multiply behind one operator.
